title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's positioning and messaging for sales conversations, short competitive briefs for common rivals, a recommended slide list and speaker notes for a 12-slide pitch deck, high-level pricing guidance, one representative case study, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this document as a single source-of-truth for field teams during discovery, demos, and procurement discussions.

Intended audience:
- Sales reps and AE's
- Solutions Engineers / Sales Engineers
- Partner and channel teams
- Customer-facing product marketers

1) Positioning & Messaging
- Core position (one-liner): Redwood Inference is the developer-first inference platform that makes high-performance, predictable LLM serving simple and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Value pillars (use these as lead-ins in discovery):
  - Production-first reliability: SLA-backed Dedicated capacity, regional redundancy, and built-in fallbacks keep customer apps online under load.
  - Predictable economics: Intelligent batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations reduce unit cost while preserving output quality.
  - Deployment choice: Start on our hosted API and seamlessly transition to dedicated or private (VPC/on-prem) without code changes.
  - Observability & control: Token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and rollout controls for safe production rollouts.
- Elevator pitches (short):
  - For engineering leaders: "Ship reliable LLM features fast — we handle the serving complexity, autoscaling, and cost optimizations so your team can focus on product work."
  - For platform teams: "Standardize inference across teams with a single API, observable performance metrics, and predictable reserved capacity for peak workloads."
  - For security/compliance buyers: "We offer private deployments, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs so you can meet enterprise security requirements without re-architecting your app."

2) Competitive briefs (one-page per competitor, quick talking points)
- Cloud-managed endpoints (major cloud providers):
  - Strengths: deep cloud integration (IAM, VPC), wide geographic regions, familiarity for infra teams.
  - Weaknesses vs Redwood: higher per-token or per-instance cost for bursty LLM workloads; less opinionated inference runtime optimizations (we provide specialized batching/kv/cache heuristics); limited graceful fallback across regions/models.
  - Win themes: predictable reserved capacity, developer ergonomics with our SDKs, cost-savings from batching/quantization suggestions, and cross-environment portability.
- LLM API providers (simplicity-first APIs):
  - Strengths: fast time-to-value, simple pricing.
  - Weaknesses vs Redwood: fewer enterprise deployment modes (private/vpc), limited capacity guarantees, less transparency into token-level cost breakdowns and performance profiling.
  - Win themes: SLA-backed Dedicated, observability, and tooling to prevent regressions in quality during model swaps.
- Self-hosted inference vendors / OSS runtimes:
  - Strengths: full control, potentially lower cost at scale.
  - Weaknesses vs Redwood: heavy engineering lift (ops, autoscaling, kernel tuning), no unified managed experience across hosted and private.
  - Win themes: Reduce ops burden, offer predictable commercial support, and provide migration path between hosted and private without code changes.

3) Pitch deck: recommended 12-slide flow and speaker notes (concise)
- Slide 1: Title + Customer logo + one-liner
  Speaker note: Short hook: latency & cost control are the real blockers to production LLM features.
- Slide 2: Problem: LLM serving complexity at scale
  Note: Highlight unpredictability of latency/cost, and quality regressions during model upgrades.
- Slide 3: Our solution: Redwood Inference (what we do)
- Slide 4: How it works (runtime + orchestration + smart routing + cache/batching)
- Slide 5: Product modes (hosted, dedicated, private) with decision matrix
- Slide 6: Performance & cost examples (benchmarks vs common baselines)
- Slide 7: Reliability features (SLA, fallbacks, A/B rollouts)
- Slide 8: Security & compliance (VPC, KMS, audit logging, SOC2)
- Slide 9: Pricing overview and commercial options (hosted usage, dedicated commits, private license)
- Slide 10: Case study snapshot (metrics and outcome)
- Slide 11: Migration & pilot plan (30/60/90 day milestones)
- Slide 12: Ask / next steps / contact
Notes for presenters: keep the first 5 minutes on customer pain, use Slide 6 to quantify expected latency/cost improvements, and keep the security slide factual with references to our compliance artifacts. Attach appendix slides for detailed SLOs, integration checklist, and sample contract terms.

4) Pricing guidance (field-level rules & examples)
- Pricing tiers (high-level):
  - Hosted API: usage-based pricing (per input token / output token / embedding unit) with free trial credits.
  - Dedicated: monthly or annual reserved capacity contracts with commit tiers; additional burst capacity at a reduced overage rate.
  - Private: commercial license + deployment fee and optional managed-support retainer.
- Field guidance:
  - Discovery: estimate expected QPS, average sequence length, and percent of requests requiring streaming or function/tool calling. Use this to model tokens/min and forecast cost.
  - Packaging: prefer a 12-month commit for Dedicated pilots above 5k QPS or predictable sustained throughput; otherwise, recommend Hosted with auto-scaling for early-stage customers.
  - Negotiation levers: commit length, reserved capacity size, SLA credits, premium onboarding, and support SLAs.
- Example pricing scenarios (illustrative):
  - SMB SaaS prototype: Hosted usage; expected 50M tokens/month; estimated monthly bill: $2.5-4k (dependent on model family).
  - Mid-market product team: Dedicated 1x T4-equivalent pool reserved; commit discount 30% vs hosted; expected saving 20-40% on token cost depending on batching and cache hit rate.
  - Regulated enterprise: Private deployment with 24/7 enterprise support; price = license + deployment + optional managed infra ($50k–$200k annual depending on footprint).
Note: do not promise specific numbers without finance approval; use these examples as a conversation guide and always route large or unusual deals to pricing@redwood.com.

5) Case study: Acme Finance (representative example)
- Customer profile: mid-market fintech product team using chat summarization and document understanding in production.
- Problem: unpredictable latency and token costs during month-end spikes; inability to meet data residency/compliance needs with a public hosted endpoint.
- Solution delivered: Dedicated pool in a regional VPC + KV prefix caching and batcher tuning; model pinned to a quantized variant with minimal latency regression.
- Outcome (30-day post-migration):
  - 99th-percentile latency reduced from 1.2s to 220ms for typical queries.
  - Monthly inference spend reduced by 36% after batching and cache tuning.
  - Compliance: successful audit evidence for data residency and KMS usage.
- Owner & contact: Sales lead — Jordan Kim; SE — Lena Zhang.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers for initial procurement conversations)
Q: What compliance certifications do you hold?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II. We provide supporting artifacts to qualified prospects under an NDA; for private deployments, customers can integrate with their on-prem audit processes.

Q: How is customer data protected in Hosted mode?
A: Data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3) and at rest (AES-256). Access controls use IAM roles scoped to customer tenants, and we offer token-level audit trails for request provenance.

Q: Do you support private deployments and VPC peering?
A: Yes. We offer a Private deployment option (VPC or on-prem) with a customer-managed control plane and options for direct network peering, VPN, or dedicated interconnect.

Q: How do you handle key management?
A: We integrate with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) and can support HSM-backed keys for private deployments. Keys can be customer-managed or hosted depending on the offering.

Q: What logging and audit capabilities are available?
A: Audit logging for control plane and request metadata is available; sensitive payload logging is disabled by default. Customers can configure retention windows and export logs to their SIEM.

Q: How do you prevent model or data leakage?
A: We use strict tenancy isolation between customers, memory scrubbing on task completion, and provide model pinning to avoid cross-tenant model updates. For high-sensitivity use cases we recommend Private deployments with network isolation.

Q: Can Redwood help with a security review / customer questionnaire?
A: Yes — our security team supports standard questionnaires (SIG, vendor risk questionnaires). Route requests to security@redwood.com and include the prospect name and the NDA status.

7) Pilot plan (recommended 30/60/90 day)
- Day 0-7: Kickoff, data access review, security questionnaire, and scope definition.
- Day 8-30: Integration & validation: API integration, sample load test, and initial performance baseline.
- Day 31-60: Optimization: apply batching/caching/quantization recommendations, implement SLO monitoring dashboards, and perform canary rollout.
- Day 61-90: Scale & handoff: finalize SLA terms, migrate traffic, and hand off to customer ops with runbooks.

8) Attachments & appendix (links to internal artifacts)
- Integration checklist (SE checklist)
- Benchmarks & perf reports (by model family & hardware)
- Pricing playbook and approved discount matrix (finance only)
- Security artifact index (SOC2 report, encryption details, network diagrams)
